title: Median Kingdom
capsule: The Median Kingdom was an Iranian imperial state centred on Ecbatana (modern Hamadan), traditionally founded by Deioces in the late 8th century BC and consolidated into a regional power by Cyaxares (r. c. 625–585 BC). In 614–612 BC Cyaxares allied with Babylonia under Nabopolassar to destroy Assyria, sacking Kalhu in 614 and Nineveh in 612 and dividing the Assyrian empire between the two powers; the Medes took the eastern territories including Urartu and much of Anatolia to the Halys River. His son Astyages (r. c. 585–550 BC) was overthrown by Cyrus II of Persia, a Median vassal, who captured Ecbatana around 550 BC and absorbed the Median nobility and administrative structure into the emerging Achaemenid Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Median Kingdom's territory is largely reconstructed from Babylonian chronicles, Herodotus, and later Achaemenid administrative texts; no Median royal inscriptions have been recovered, so boundaries — especially in the east and northeast — are conjectural.
